newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Endemol says faces no Sport7 losses.
newsitem.headline: Endemol says faces no Sport7 losses.

text.p: Dutch television production company Endemol Entertainment Holding said on Wednesday its management would personally bear any bad debt losses arising from the collapse of sports-only television channel Sport7, a major client.
"Messrs John de Mol and Joop van den Ende will personally make good any losses Endemol might incur through the non-payment of bills by Sport7," Endemol spokesman Thomas Notermans said.
Sport7 was granted court protection from creditors on Tuesday.
Notermans said that the collapsed channel owed Endemol Entertainment some 33 million guilders for programmes supplied.
"Endemol Sport BV is Sport7's biggest creditor, with bills outstanding of some 26 million guilders," Notermans said.
Operating companies Joop van den Ende Television Productions and John de Mol productions were owed around 2.5 and 4.0 million guilders respectively, he added.
He said the bulk of the money was expected to be paid out when Sport7 was wound up, with Van den Ende and De Mol making up any difference.
Endemol said on Sunday Sport7's collapse would have no effect on its profit forecast for the 1996/97 financial year ending July 31, 1997.

"The company still anticipates that revenue and net earnings will grow by between 15 and 20 percent in the current financial year...as was forecast at the presentation of Endemol's annual figures," Endemol said in a statement.
Shares in the bourse newcomer surged in late November after the company announced it had sold its 19.5 percent stake in Sport7 to Van den Ende and De Mol.
